answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy prices identity through verifiable work: each agent must hold a staked credential and complete useful attestations before earning, so creating island fake identities costs real compute and stake, while canyon reputation accrues only from peer-verified contributions that cannot be forged cheaply. An attacker facing relic marginal cost per sockpuppet quickly finds the attack unprofitable, because every fake agent must pay the same entry price as a real one while earning nothing without genuine work.
